This study timed loops and programs with checks off and on: a different measurement, so it neither confirms nor contradicts Google's average.
Loops that lose SIMD are rare in the general libraries counted and not rare in the numeric projects (counted, not timed).
- **Real programs** (four projects) were picked because they contain lost loops, not sampled.

- **Rules were loosened after seeing results.** The day-one test (the first two runs) judged forward loops by a rule that both runs failed, so the result was no-go as written; the rule was then relaxed in `harness/criteria.json`.

The later versions (v2, v3) changed no threshold but added rules (the aligned column, the layout A/A, placement-sensitive cells, pooling per CPU model, 40 repetitions per side) after earlier results were known, so they are not pre-registered.
Inferred from knowledge of the LLVM source, not observed: that the vectorizer requires the count, and the rule that gives the stride-2 checks none.
